Bug_Title: STI: Unneeded use of currentThread() call, to call interrupted() (STI_INTERRUPTED_ON_CURRENTTHREAD)
Bug_Details:
This method invokes the Thread.currentThread() call, just to call the
interrupted() method. As interrupted() is a static method, it is more
simple and clear to use Thread.interrupted().
 Thread.currentThread() interrupted() interrupted() Thread.interrupted()
Bug_Explanation: The code unnecessarily uses Thread.currentThread() to call the interrupted() method. Since interrupted() is a static method, it should be called directly using Thread.interrupted() for clarity and simplicity.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test case calls the showBug method, which uses Thread.currentThread().interrupted() to check the interrupted status of the current thread. Since the method unnecessarily uses Thread.currentThread().interrupted() instead of the simpler Thread.interrupted(), the test case will fail if the interrupted status of the current thread is not false. This demonstrates the bug, because the current thread was not interrupted, but the method uses an incorrect check.
Test_Run_Result: Runninng test will fail system because of infinite loop.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results indicate an infinite loop, which suggests that the use of Thread.currentThread().interrupted() is causing unexpected behavior. This aligns with the bug description of unnecessary use of currentThread() to call interrupted(), confirming the bug is triggered.
